intro: When you search for a commercial conveyancer near me, you're likely dealing with a shop, office, industrial unit or investment property rather than your home. You want someone local who understands the extra layers of commercial property work, from VAT to lease terms. iComply introduces you to a suitable UK conveyancer who can quote you directly for the job.
need_heading: What people searching for a commercial conveyancer near me usually need
need_lead: Commercial conveyancing covers a wider range of issues than buying a house, so it helps to know what you're stepping into.
needs: You are buying or selling a shop, office or industrial unit and need a conveyancer who regularly handles commercial property rather than only residential homes.
You are taking on a lease for business premises and want the terms reviewed carefully before you commit to rent and repairing obligations.
You are a landlord or investor and need the purchase or sale of a tenanted commercial property handled with proper due diligence.
You want a conveyancer based near you so you can discuss documents in person and have someone familiar with the local commercial market.
You are unsure whether VAT applies to the property transaction and need clear guidance on how it affects the deal.
context_heading: Why local knowledge matters for commercial conveyancing
context: Commercial conveyancers deal with the purchase, sale and leasing of shops, offices, industrial units and investment property. Because commercial property often involves VAT, longer lease terms and more detailed due diligence than a residential purchase, you want a conveyancer who works in this area regularly and is easy to reach when questions come up.

Conveyancing in England and Wales is a reserved legal activity, carried out either by solicitors regulated by the Solicitors Regulation Authority or by licensed conveyancers regulated by the Council for Licensed Conveyancers. Both must hold professional indemnity insurance and follow strict rules on handling client money. In Scotland, property transactions are handled by solicitors under Scottish law.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Whether you are buying, selling or leasing a commercial property, and what type of premises it is, such as a shop, office or industrial unit.
The approximate location of the property so we can introduce you to a conveyancer near you.
Whether the property is already tenanted or you plan to occupy it yourself, as this affects the work involved.
Any tight deadlines you are working towards, such as a lease start date or a deal that needs to complete quickly.
Whether VAT is likely to be an issue on the transaction, so the conveyancer can advise you from the start.
If you have a lender involved, mention it, as some lenders require conveyancers to be on their panel.
questions_heading: Questions to ask the commercial conveyancer
questions: How often do you handle commercial property transactions like mine?
What is your approach to reviewing lease terms and advising on repairing obligations?
How will you deal with VAT on this transaction and what should I be aware of?
What does your due diligence cover for a commercial property that is different from a residential purchase?
Are you on my lender's panel if I am using finance for this purchase?
How will you keep me updated on progress and who will be my main point of contact?

faqs.q: Do I need a commercial conveyancer rather than a residential one?
faqs.a: Commercial property transactions involve different issues such as VAT, lease terms and wider due diligence, so it is sensible to use a conveyancer who regularly deals with commercial work. A residential conveyancer may not have the same experience with these matters.

faqs.q: Can you introduce me to a conveyancer near my business?
faqs.a: Yes, iComply introduces people to suitable UK conveyancers based on the details you provide, including location. You then deal directly with the conveyancer, who will quote you for the work.

faqs.q: What does 'price on application' mean for a commercial conveyancer?
faqs.a: It means the conveyancer will quote you based on the specifics of your transaction rather than advertising a fixed price. Commercial property work varies widely, so a tailored quote is common.

faqs.q: How do I check a conveyancer is properly regulated?
faqs.a: In England and Wales, you can check whether a conveyancer is regulated by the Solicitors Regulation Authority or the Council for Licensed Conveyancers. In Scotland, solicitors are regulated under Scottish law.

extra_heading: What 'near me' means for commercial conveyancing
extra: When you search for a commercial conveyancer near me, you may be imagining a high-street office where you can drop in with a folder of documents. Many commercial conveyancers now work remotely and serve clients across the country, so 'near me' might mean someone who is easy to reach by phone or email and who understands the local commercial property market, rather than a firm on your doorstep.

A local conveyancer can be helpful if you want to discuss plans in person or if they already know the area where your shop, office or industrial unit is located. But don't overlook a firm slightly further afield if they specialise in the type of commercial property you're dealing with, such as a retail lease or an investment purchase, and can explain the process clearly.

Before you instruct anyone, check that they are regulated by the Solicitors Regulation Authority or the Council for Licensed Conveyancers, and ask whether they are on your lender's panel if you are using finance. iComply introduces you to a suitable UK conveyancer who will quote you directly, with the price on application, so you can compare what's offered and decide for yourself.

extra_faqs.q: Do I have to choose a conveyancer based near the property?
extra_faqs.a: Not necessarily. Commercial conveyancers can act for you from anywhere in England and Wales, and much of the work is done by phone, email and post. What matters most is their experience with commercial property and that you can communicate easily with them.

extra_faqs.q: How can I compare commercial conveyancers near me?
extra_faqs.a: Ask each conveyancer about their experience with transactions like yours, how they will handle VAT and lease terms, and what their quote includes. Since quotes are on application, you can compare the scope of work and the clarity of their explanation, not just the price.
